new_statements.quote: Suprasegmentals (tone, stress, length) Stress is difficult to detect and it is subordinate to length. Stress seems to fall on the last syllable of the root in most cases.
new_statements.citation: SIL PNG Branch. n.d. [2004 PDF; based on Voltmer, Brad & Deb Voltmer 1994 ms.]. Saep Organised Phonology Data. SIL Language & Culture Archives no. 42388, 4 pp.
new_statements.second_reader_evidence: File checked: (4 pp., the PDF's metadata gives the Title 'OPD', Author 'SIL PNG Branch', created 2004-09-05; text present, is a faithful extracted text). On p.3, under the heading 'Suprasegmentals (tone, stress, length)', the text reads exactly: 'Stress is difficult to detect and it is subordinate to length. Stress seems to fall on the last syllable of the root in most cases.' -- verbatim as quoted. Surrounding context read: the sheet gives consonant/vowel inventories with example words (no stress marks anywhere), a vowel-length series written with double letters (ii ee aa oo uu; 'Lengthened vowels are written with double letters'), syllable patterns, phonological/orthographic conventions,…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Weak, hard-to-hear stress, tentatively on the final syllable of the root (i.e. root-final, not necessarily word-final once suffixes are added); vowel length is contrastive and perceptually dominates stress. The statement is hedged ('seems', 'in most cases') and the domain is the root, so 'morphologically determined'/root-final is an equally defensible reading; fixed: final syllable chosen as the positional rule within the root.
new_statements.exceptions: Only the hedge 'in most cases'; no exceptions listed. Length (written with double vowels aa, ee, ii, oo, uu) is treated as the primary suprasegmental.
new_statements.domain_note: Domain stated as the root ('last syllable of the root'), implying suffixes (e.g. verb endings -ba, possessive -gou) are unstressed; no discussion of phrase level or citation forms. 4-page OPD sheet, draft posted without peer review.
new_statements.identity_note: Source is explicitly 'Saep Language [SPD]', Rai Coast Stock, Yaganon Family, Madang Province (villages Buff, Ibe, Olinma, Ayoak, Segi, Budamu; pop. 584) = Glottolog saep1240. No dialect distinctions made.
